title: Hamlet home — one functional cutaway room
status: proposed visual direction; no external art copied
thesis: Make one sunlit, open-front domestic room that reads as a hand-built miniature. Each useful Hamlet action is attached to a distinct piece of furniture, while one clear inner loop leaves the bean room to arrive, pause and act.

source_notes.name: Unpacking — official site, Witch Beam
source_notes.observed: The official description foregrounds fitting possessions into a home, domestic nooks, and learning a life through the things that remain.
source_notes.translation: Use possessions as quiet evidence of function: a single red envelope at the mail tray, clipped lesson sheets, a half-used pencil cup and one folded throw. Avoid decorative clutter without a job.

source_notes.name: Tiny Glade — official page, Pounce Light
source_notes.observed: Pounce Light calls Tiny Glade a relaxing diorama builder for whimsical castles, cottages and ruins.
source_notes.translation: Favor readable, generous silhouette, irregular hand-made details and soft outdoor light over a dense simulation of an interior.

source_notes.name: Mark Turpin — official architectural-miniature portfolio
source_notes.observed: The artist documents one-of-a-kind miniature houses, structures and room settings.
source_notes.translation: Give the room a deliberate display-object edge: substantial plinth, wall thickness, millwork depth and a framed cutaway boundary rather than invisible game walls.

source_notes.name: Gooyland — official miniature-worlds studio
source_notes.observed: The studio describes fully hand-carved, sculpted and wired miniature worlds, from a detail vignette to a complete room.
source_notes.translation: Reserve fine detail for a few tactile points: peg rail, paper edge, ceramic planter, brass lamp and visible wood joinery. Light should make those points legible.

composition.camera: Orthographic, yaw 45 degrees, pitch 35.2644 degrees below horizontal. Open the front and right walls. Crop the back-left corner near the upper third; keep the window just left of centre.
composition.logical_size: 7.8 W × 6.2 D × 4.4 H scene units; floor slab 0.28 H and wall thickness 0.20.
composition.movement_clearance: Keep a 1.05-unit loop from entry threshold to mail tray, desk, workbench and sofa. Do not put props in the loop. Bean body diameter is about 0.60; interaction points must leave 0.85 clear around the bean.
composition.cutaway_edges: Use 0.10–0.14 chamfers only on plinth, sill and furniture hand-contact edges. Keep walls and large shelves crisp so the room does not melt into a toy blob.

functional_objects.placement: At the entrance, on a narrow shoe-and-mail console facing into the room.
functional_objects.geometry: 0.92 W × 0.62 D × 0.88 H oak console; shallow terracotta tray, upright postcard slot, 3 brass hooks above.
functional_objects.interaction: Bean arrives from the threshold, pauses beside the tray, lifts one envelope; tray gets a faint warm rim only when mail is ready.
functional_objects.story_prop: One stamped envelope and a small key bowl; never a stack of generic letters.

functional_objects.placement: On the back wall, visible above the workbench without competing with the window.
functional_objects.geometry: 1.22 W × 0.82 H linen board in an oak rail; 3–5 paper tiles at 0.03 depth, dark green round pins.
functional_objects.interaction: Bean turns toward it; one note can lift 0.03 and settle. The active note becomes warm paper, not a neon state.
functional_objects.story_prop: Two tilted cards, one clipped receipt-size note, one small dried-leaf marker.

functional_objects.placement: Under the window, rotated slightly toward the view; the chair faces the window and leaves the aisle open behind it.
functional_objects.geometry: 1.42 W × 0.68 D × 0.74 H desk; arched-back chair 0.54 W; small mushroom lamp and two stacked books.
functional_objects.interaction: Bean steps onto a low footstool, opens a lesson folio and settles into a tiny idle bob. Lamp warms to 2700 K when studying.
functional_objects.story_prop: One pencil, one open folio, one cup with pens. Keep the desktop mostly clear.

functional_objects.placement: Along the left wall beneath the pinboard, perpendicular to the desk to make an L-shaped productive corner.
functional_objects.geometry: 1.68 W × 0.76 D × 0.92 H butcher-block bench; peg rail, two small drawers, cork stamp, blue sketchbook and clay cup.
functional_objects.interaction: Bean reaches up to set a sketchbook or stamp down. A drafted idea is a small paper plane / folded-card animation, never an abstract particle cloud.
functional_objects.story_prop: Three peg silhouettes and one imperfect hand-cut swatch give it craft without becoming a workshop set.

functional_objects.placement: Front-right, angled 12 degrees inward; it frames the room without blocking the entry-to-desk loop.
functional_objects.geometry: 1.62 W × 0.76 D × 0.72 H low sage sofa; two cushions, folded ochre throw, round side table.
functional_objects.interaction: Bean climbs via a 0.18-high ottoman, tucks into the left cushion and breathes slowly. No completion or productivity signal appears.
functional_objects.story_prop: A mug or closed book, selected by state, but only one at a time.

architectural: floor slab with visible birch-ply edge
kit.micro_detail_budget: At 1080p, make 8–12 details visibly resolve: window latch, curtain tie, lamp shade, paper stack, tray lip, pin heads, peg rail, drawer pull, cushion seam and planter rim. Let smaller items merge into grouped shapes.

plaster.use: walls; add only a 2–3% warm variation

terracotta.use: mail tray and small ceramic accent

lighting.day: Area key through the window from upper left, warm 5100 K, broad 3.2-unit source, soft shadows. Cool sky fill at 15–20% of key. Add a small negative fill behind the sofa if it flattens.
lighting.practical: Desk lamp uses a 2700 K point/area light with a small radius and is off until study. Do not light every shelf.
lighting.contact: Use short local contact shadow only below furniture, inside the tray and under the sill. Avoid global dirt or a long AO fog.
lighting.tone: ACES or equivalent gentle rolloff; avoid bloom. White plaster should remain cream, never clip to pure white.

motion.idle: Curtain shifts 1–2 degrees over 5–7 seconds; dust motes are optional and must be nearly invisible; bean breathes at 3–4% vertical scale over 1.8 seconds.
motion.walk: Use 6–8 very short waypoints around the central loop. Move at 0.55–0.70 scene units/s, with a brief 0.35 s stop at each interaction point. Turn first, then translate, so the bean reads as intentional.
motion.reduced_motion: Keep the scene still, retain state through one material/value change, and do not auto-walk the bean.

build_order: Block the plinth, two walls, window and walkable loop in clay. Check that all five functions can be pointed to without text.
Place desk, workbench and sofa; reserve the bean's 1.05-unit loop before adding any props.
Add the functional affordances: tray, pinboard, folio, sketchbook and ottoman.
Tune window key, contact shadows and material roughness in an untextured render.
Add the small crafted details last. Remove any detail that does not clarify scale, touch or use.
avoid: A row of labelled stations around the wall: that makes a feature menu, not a home.
Uniform rounding on every object, high saturation, black outlines or bloom used to force legibility.
A glassless window or invisible light source; the daylight needs a believable origin and sill depth.
Tight prop clusters in the bean's loop, long furniture runs without rests, or a sofa that blocks the door.
Productivity trophies, score effects or a special reward for resting.
